planting.note: Set container plants out in spring or fall in well-drained soil; this compact native ninebark holds its chartreuse color best with a full day of sun and needs little upkeep once roots are established.

directions: This dwarf ninebark pushes bright chartreuse new growth each spring and stays densely covered in small white flower clusters along every stem. It tolerates drought, poor soil, and harsh winters once established, making it a low-fuss choice for cold climates. Little to no pruning is required beyond an occasional thinning cut to maintain shape. Use it as a compact accent or informal low hedge where a tough, reliable native shrub is needed.

planting.note: Plant in part shade to full sun in average, well-drained soil; this low mounding deutzia blooms on old wood so it rarely needs pruning beyond removing spent flowering stems.

directions: Yuki Kabuki produces a dense mass of small pink-and-white bell-shaped flowers over a naturally rounded, tidy mound each spring. The medium green summer foliage shifts to a glossy burgundy in autumn, adding a second season of interest. It fits comfortably into mixed borders, low hedges, or containers without outgrowing its space. Established plants tolerate drought and resist deer, flowering reliably with minimal intervention.

planting.note: Space plants on their wider spread rather than the original cultivar's tighter footprint; grows well as a dense, shrubby groundcover in sun to part sun with good drainage.

directions: This update to the original Yuki Cherry Blossom deutzia keeps the same low, mounding habit and two-toned pink-and-white spring flowers along burgundy stems, but spreads noticeably wider for better ground coverage. Its dense habit helps crowd out weeds while the green summer foliage turns a strong fall color before frost. It is well suited to edging, slopes, or mass planting where a very low, spreading flowering shrub is wanted. Established plants need little care beyond occasional shaping.

planting.note: Tolerates everything from full sun to full shade and most soils except those that stay wet; give some direct sun for the best foliage color.

directions: Kodiak Fresh is a compact native bush honeysuckle whose new growth opens in orange tones before settling into a bright lime-green that holds its color through summer heat. Small clusters of tubular yellow flowers appear continuously from early summer into fall, drawing bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds. It handles dry shade better than most flowering shrubs, though a few hours of direct sun sharpens the foliage color and fall display. Rejuvenation pruning every few years keeps the mounding habit tidy.

planting.note: Give full sun and well-drained soil with room to reach full size; works well as a specimen, screen, or informal hedge in larger landscapes.

directions: Ruffled Satin bears large, ruffled pink flowers with a dramatic burgundy-red central eye, opening in overlapping layers that give the bloom a cupped, full-petaled look. Flowering runs from early through late summer on a vigorous, upright shrub well suited to screening or specimen use. It tolerates heat and average garden soil once established and needs only minimal shaping in early spring. Deadheading is unnecessary for repeat bloom, though removing spent flowers can tidy its appearance.

common_name: Dark Lavender Chiffon Rose of Sharon

planting.note: Plant in full sun in soil that is neither constantly wet nor very dry; prune lightly in early spring if a more compact shape is wanted.

directions: Dark Lavender Chiffon is the richest-colored member of the Chiffon rose of sharon series, producing deep purple semi-double, ruffled blooms over glossy green foliage from midsummer into fall. Its upright, rounded form sets very few seed pods, limiting the self-seeding that troubles many older rose of sharon cultivars. Established plants shrug off heat, drought, and salt exposure, and are rarely bothered by deer. Use it as a flowering screen, informal hedge, or tall border accent in sunny sites.
